rationale: A has the clearer evaluator architecture: definitions are compiled by a dedicated helper, token execution is uniform, and its parser supports definitions and ordinary expressions occurring together on a line, including trailing tokens and multiple definitions. B is readable and centralizes errors well, but its line-oriented special case only recognizes a definition when ':' is the first token and requires ';' to be the final token, making it unnecessarily restrictive and less robust; its popOne name is also misleading because it only peeks.
